column1: # Reviewed exceptions to public_check rules.
# Format, tab separated:
#   path-glob <TAB> rule-id <TAB> exact-matched-text <TAB> reason
# Use "*" as the matched text to suppress a rule for a whole path glob. Prefer
# an exact match: a broad suppression hides the next real finding.
# Every line needs a reason. An entry with no reason is a mute, not a review.
# EMPTY, ON PURPOSE.
# This file previously carried five entries suppressing an employer-name rule
# where a bare capitalized word meant "meta-level" rather than a company. Every
# one of those was resolved by editing the source text to say what it meant
# ("Meta-level preferences", "meta-framing"), which is a real fix. The
# suppressions were then deleted.
# Two reasons not to bring them back:
#  1. Generalizing the text removes the token from the published repo. An
#     allowlist entry leaves it there and asserts it is fine.
#  2. The entry has to quote the string it suppresses, so an allowlist for a
#     private value publishes that value in this file, which is tracked.
# So: never allowlist a private value. Rewrite the text instead. Add an entry
# here only for a genuine shape false positive that cannot be reworded, and give
# it a reason a stranger can check.
